22: 
23: #define MB_PHY_CMD_CHNL		(MAILBOX_BOX0)
24: #define MB_PHY_ACK_CHNL		(MAILBOX_BOX1)
25: 
26: #define CHNL_STATE_BUSY		1
27: #define CHNL_STATE_IDLE		0
28: 
29: /* If a physical channel stays BUSY longer than this (in milliseconds)
30:  * without seeing the matching ACK from the peer CPU, mb_chnl_write() will
31:  * forcibly recover it. Normal mailbox round-trips are << 1 ms, so 200 ms
32:  * is well clear of any legitimate burst while still keeping the system
33:  * responsive in the unlikely event the peer never replies. */
34: #define MB_PHY_CHNL_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS		200
35: 
36: typedef struct
37: {
38: 	volatile u8		tx_state;	/* physical channel tx state. */
39: 	u8		tx_seq;				/* physical channel tx sequence. */
40: 	u8		tx_log_chnl;		/* logical channel. */ /* bit7~bit4: dst/src CPU_ID, bit3~bit0: log_chnl_idx. */
41: 	u8		tx_hdr_cmd;
42: 	u32		rx_fault_cnt;
43: 	u32		tx_fault_cnt;
44: 	/* Wall-clock (ms via rtos_get_time()) at which tx_state was set to
45: 	 * CHNL_STATE_BUSY. Used by mb_chnl_write() to detect a physical
46: 	 * channel that has been BUSY abnormally long (peer lost / dropped
47: 	 * the ACK) and forcibly clear it. 0 means "channel is IDLE". */
48: 	volatile u32	busy_since_ms;
49: } mb_phy_chnl_cb_t;
50: 
51: 
52: #define CHNL_CTRL_MASK			0xF
53: /*
54:  *  there are 2 boxes in one MAILBOXn HW,
55:  *  but no way to know which box this msg is from in current mailbox_driver design.
56:  *  use the CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX bit in the msg hdr.ctrl to distinguish where it is from.
57:  *  when CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX is set, it means from ack box ( MAILBOXn_BOX1 ).
58:  */
59: #define CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX		0x01
60: 
61: #define CHNL_CTRL_SYNC_TX		0x02
62: #define CHNL_CTRL_RESET			0x04
63: 
64: typedef union
65: {
66: 	struct
67: 	{
68: 		u32		cmd            : 8;
69: 		u32		state          : 4;
70: 		u32		ctrl           : 4;
71: 		u32		tx_seq         : 8;
72: 		u32		logical_chnl   : 8;
73: 	} ;
74: 	u32		data;
75: } phy_chnnl_hdr_t;
76: 
77: typedef struct
78: {
79: 	phy_chnnl_hdr_t	hdr;
80: 
81: 	u32		param1;
82: 	u32		param2;
83: 	u32		param3;
84: } mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t;
85: 
86: typedef struct
87: {
88: 	phy_chnnl_hdr_t	hdr;
89: 
90: 	u32		data1;
91: 	u32		data2;
92: 	u32		data3;
93: } mb_phy_chnl_ack_t;
94: 
95: typedef union
96: {
97: 	phy_chnnl_hdr_t		phy_ch_hdr;
98: 	mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t	phy_ch_cmd;
99: 	mb_phy_chnl_ack_t	phy_ch_ack;
100: 	mailbox_data_t		mb_data;
101: } mb_phy_chnl_union_t;
102: 
103: typedef struct
104: {
105: 	volatile u8		tx_state;				/* logical channel tx state. */
106: 	u8				in_used;
107: 	chnl_rx_isr_t		rx_isr;
108: 	chnl_tx_isr_t		tx_isr;
109: 	chnl_tx_cmpl_isr_t	tx_cmpl_isr;
110: 	void *				isr_param;
111: 	mailbox_data_t		chnnl_tx_buff;		/* logical channel tx buffer. */
112: } mb_log_chnl_cb_t;
113: 
114: #define PHY_CHNL_NUM		SYSTEM_CPU_NUM
115: 
116: static mb_phy_chnl_cb_t		phy_chnl_x_cb[PHY_CHNL_NUM];
117: static mb_log_chnl_cb_t		log_chnl_cb0[CP0_MB_LOG_CHNL_END - CP0_MB_LOG_CHNL_START];
118: static mb_log_chnl_cb_t		log_chnl_cb1[CP1_MB_LOG_CHNL_END - CP1_MB_LOG_CHNL_START];
119: #if PHY_CHNL_NUM > 2
120: static mb_log_chnl_cb_t		log_chnl_cb2[CP2_MB_LOG_CHNL_END - CP2_MB_LOG_CHNL_START];
121: #endif
122: #if PHY_CHNL_NUM > 3
123: static mb_log_chnl_cb_t		log_chnl_cb3[CP3_MB_LOG_CHNL_END - CP3_MB_LOG_CHNL_START];
124: #endif
125: 
126: static const u8 	phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[PHY_CHNL_NUM] = { 
127: 	ARRAY_SIZE(log_chnl_cb0),
128: 	ARRAY_SIZE(log_chnl_cb1),
129: #if PHY_CHNL_NUM > 2
130: 	ARRAY_SIZE(log_chnl_cb2),
131: #endif
132: #if PHY_CHNL_NUM > 3
133: 	ARRAY_SIZE(log_chnl_cb3),
134: #endif
135: //	CP0_MB_LOG_CHNL_END - CP0_MB_LOG_CHNL_START, 
136: 	};
137: 
138: static const mb_log_chnl_cb_t *	phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[PHY_CHNL_NUM] = {
139: 	&log_chnl_cb0[0], 
140: 	&log_chnl_cb1[0], 
141: #if PHY_CHNL_NUM > 2
142: 	&log_chnl_cb2[0], 
143: #endif
144: #if PHY_CHNL_NUM > 3
145: 	&log_chnl_cb3[0], 
146: #endif
147: 	};
148: 
149: static u8				mb_chnnl_init_ok = 0;
150: 
151: #if CONFIG_SOC_SMP
152: #include "spinlock.h"
153: static SPINLOCK_SECTION volatile spinlock_t mb_chnl_spin_lock = SPIN_LOCK_INIT;
154: #endif // CONFIG_SOC_SMP
155: static inline uint32_t mb_chnl_enter_critical()
156: {
157: 	uint32_t flags = rtos_disable_int();
158: 
159: #if CONFIG_SOC_SMP
160: 	spin_lock(&mb_chnl_spin_lock);
161: #endif // CONFIG_SOC_SMP
162: 
163: 	return flags;
164: }
165: 
166: static inline void mb_chnl_exit_critical(uint32_t flags)
167: {
168: #if CONFIG_SOC_SMP
169: 	spin_unlock(&mb_chnl_spin_lock);
170: #endif // CONFIG_SOC_SMP
171: 
172: 	rtos_enable_int(flags);
173: }
174: 
175: /* =====================      physical channel functions      ==================*/
176: static volatile uint32_t s_mailbox_tx_cnt = 0;
177: static volatile uint32_t s_mailbox_rx_cnt = 0;
178: static volatile uint32_t s_mailbox_rx_ack_cnt = 0;
179: 
180: static volatile uint32_t s_mailbox_tx_ack_cnt = 0;
181: static volatile uint32_t s_mailbox_tx_compl_cnt = 0;
182: 
183: static inline bk_err_t bk_mailbox_send_safe(mailbox_data_t *data, mailbox_endpoint_t src, mailbox_endpoint_t dst, void *arg)
184: {
185: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;
186: 	
187: 	u32 int_mask = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
188: 	ret_code = bk_mailbox_send(data, src, dst, arg);
189: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
190: 	
191: 	return ret_code;
192: }
193: 
194: static u8 mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd(u8 log_chnl)
195: {
196: 	mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t	* cmd_ptr;
197: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;
198: 	u16 			chnl_type;
199: 	u8				phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
200: 	u8				log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
201: 
202: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
203: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
204: 
205: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
206: 		return 4;
207: 
208: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // transferred to self.
209: 		return 5;
210: 
211: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
212: 		return 3;
213: 
214: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
215: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
216: 
217: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
218: 		return 1;
219: 
220: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_seq++;
221: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_log_chnl = log_chnl;
222: 
223: 	cmd_ptr = (mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t *)&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff;
224: 
225: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = log_chnl;
226: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.tx_seq = phy_chnl_ptr->tx_seq;
227: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl  = 0;
228: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.state = 0;
229: 
230: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_hdr_cmd = cmd_ptr->hdr.cmd;
231: 
232: 	__DMB();
233: 	chnl_type = MB_PHY_CMD_CHNL;
234: 
235: 	mailbox_endpoint_t    dst_cpu = (mailbox_endpoint_t)(phy_chnl_idx);
236: 
237: 	ret_code = bk_mailbox_send(&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff, SELF_CPU, dst_cpu, (void *)&chnl_type);
238: 
239: 	if(ret_code != BK_OK)
240: 	{
241: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt++;
242: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt |= 0x40000000;
243: 
244: 		return 2;
245: 	}
246: 
247: 	log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
248: 
249: 	s_mailbox_tx_cnt++;
250: 
251: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_isr != NULL)
252: 	{
253: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_isr(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param);  	/* phy_chnl is BUSY now, tx_isr will not trigger phy_chnl_start_tx. */
254: 	}
255: 
256: 	return 0;
257: }
258: 
259: static void mb_phy_chnl_rx_ack_isr(mb_phy_chnl_ack_t *ack_ptr)
260: {
261: 	u8		log_chnl;
262: 	u8		ret_code;
263: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx;
264: 	u8		log_chnl_idx;
265: 
266: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
267: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
268: 
269: 	log_chnl = ack_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl;
270: 
271: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
272: 	log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
273: 
274: 	s_mailbox_tx_ack_cnt++;
275: 
276: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
277: 		return;
278: 
279: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // received from self.
280: 		return;
281: 
282: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
283: 		return;
284: 
285: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
286: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
287: 
288: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
289: 		return;
290: 
291: 	if( (log_chnl != phy_chnl_ptr->tx_log_chnl) ||
292: 		(ack_ptr->hdr.tx_seq != phy_chnl_ptr->tx_seq) )
293: 	{
294: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt++;
295: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt |= 0x40000000;
296: 
297: 		/* Stale / mismatched ACK. The original implementation just
298: 		 * returned here, which left phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state stuck at
299: 		 * BUSY forever and deadlocked all subsequent mb_chnl_write()
300: 		 * on this physical channel. Recover the channel and re-dispatch
301: 		 * any pending logical-channel tx so we don't lose the link. */
302: 		{
303: 			u32 int_mask_stale = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
304: 			u8  i;
305: 
306: 			phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state      = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
307: 			phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = 0;
308: 
309: 			for (i = 0; i < phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx]; i++) {
310: 				if (log_chnl_cb_x[i].tx_state != CHNL_STATE_IDLE) {
311: 					u8 pending = CPX_LOG_CHNL_START(SELF_CPU, phy_chnl_idx) + i;
312: 					phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state      = CHNL_STATE_BUSY;
313: 					phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = rtos_get_time();
314: 					if (mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd(pending) != 0) {
315: 						log_chnl_cb_x[i].tx_state   = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
316: 						phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state      = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
317: 						phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = 0;
318: 					}
319: 					break;
320: 				}
321: 			}
322: 			mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask_stale);
323: 		}
324: 		return;
325: 	}
326: 
327: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_cmpl_isr != NULL)
328: 	{
329: 		/* clear following header members. */
330: 		ack_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = 0;
331: 		ack_ptr->hdr.tx_seq       = 0;
332: 		ack_ptr->hdr.ctrl         = 0;
333: 
334: 		/* hdr.state, hdr.cmd these 2 members keep untouched. */
335: 
336: 		s_mailbox_tx_compl_cnt++;
337: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_cmpl_isr(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param, (mb_chnl_ack_t *)ack_ptr);
338: 	}
339: 
340: 	u32 int_mask = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
341: 	for(log_chnl_idx = 0; log_chnl_idx < phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx]; log_chnl_idx++)  /* priority descended search. */
342: 	{
343: 		if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state != CHNL_STATE_IDLE)
344: 			break;
345: 	}
346: 
347: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
348: 	{
349: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state      = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
350: 		phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = 0;
351: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
352: 		return;
353: 	}
354: 
355: 	log_chnl = CPX_LOG_CHNL_START(SELF_CPU, phy_chnl_idx) + log_chnl_idx;
356: 
357: 	/* About to dispatch the next pending tx on this physical channel:
358: 	 * refresh the busy-watchdog timestamp so its lifetime starts from
359: 	 * here rather than carrying over from the previous transaction. */
360: 	phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = rtos_get_time();
361: 
362: 	ret_code = mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd(log_chnl);
363: 
364: 	if(ret_code != 0)
365: 	{
366: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
367: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state               = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
368: 		phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms          = 0;
369: 	}
370: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
371: 
372: 	return;
373: 
374: }

376: static void mb_phy_chnl_rx_cmd_isr(mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t *cmd_ptr)
377: {
378: 	phy_chnnl_hdr_t  chnl_hdr;
379: 	u8			log_chnl = cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl;
380: 	bk_err_t	ret_code;
381: 	u16 		chnl_type;
382: 
383: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx;
384: 	u8		log_chnl_idx;
385: 
386: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
387: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
388: 
389: 	s_mailbox_rx_cnt++;
390: 
391: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = SRC_CPU_ID; from SRC_CPU.
392: 	log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
393: 
394: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
395: 		return;
396: 
397: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // received from self.
398: 		return;
399: 
400: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
401: 		return;
402: 
403: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
404: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
405: 
406: 	chnl_hdr.data = cmd_ptr->hdr.data;
407: 
408: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
409: 	{
410: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt++;
411: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt |= 0x80000000;
412: 
413: 		return;
414: 	}
415: 
416: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].rx_isr != NULL)
417: 	{
418: 		/* clear all other hdr members except hdr.cmd. */
419: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = 0;
420: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.tx_seq       = 0;
421: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl         = 0;
422: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.state        = 0;
423: 
424: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].rx_isr(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param, (mb_chnl_cmd_t *)cmd_ptr);
425: 
426: 		/* !!!! cmd_ptr buffer now contains ACK data !!!!. */
427: 	}
428: 	else
429: 	{
430: 		chnl_hdr.state |= CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL;		/* cmd NO target app, it is an ACK bit to peer CPU. */
431: 	}
432: 
433: 	if(chnl_hdr.ctrl & CHNL_CTRL_SYNC_TX)
434: 	{
435: 		/* sync tx cmd, do NOT send ACK. */
436: 		return;
437: 	}
438: 
439: 	/* mb_phy_chnl_tx_ack. */
440: 
441: 	/* RE-USE the cmd buffer for ACK !!! */
442: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.data  = chnl_hdr.data;
443: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl |= CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX;			/* ACK msg, use the ACK channel.  */
444: 
445: 	chnl_type = MB_PHY_ACK_CHNL;
446: 
447: 	mailbox_endpoint_t    dst_cpu = (mailbox_endpoint_t)(phy_chnl_idx);
448: 
449: 	ret_code = bk_mailbox_send_safe((mailbox_data_t *)cmd_ptr, SELF_CPU, dst_cpu, (void *)&chnl_type);	/* mb_phy_chnl_tx_ack. */
450: 
451: 	if(ret_code != BK_OK)
452: 	{
453: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt++;
454: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt |= 0x80000000;
455: 
456: 		return;
457: 	}
458: 	s_mailbox_rx_ack_cnt++;
459: 	return;
460: }

462: static void mb_phy_chnl_rx_isr(mailbox_data_t * mb_data)
463: {
464: 	mb_phy_chnl_union_t	rx_data;
465: 
466: 	rx_data.mb_data.param0 = mb_data->param0;
467: 	rx_data.mb_data.param1 = mb_data->param1;
468: 	rx_data.mb_data.param2 = mb_data->param2;
469: 	rx_data.mb_data.param3 = mb_data->param3;
470: 	/* the following process will damage the input parameter,
471: 	so pass in the pointer of copied parameter instad of the original. */
472: 
473: 	/*
474: 	 *  there are 2 boxes in one MAILBOXn HW,
475: 	 *  but no way to know which box this msg is from in current mailbox_driver design.
476: 	 *  so use the CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX bit in the msg hdr.ctrl to distinguish where it is from.
477: 	 *  when CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX is set, it means from ack box ( MAILBOXn_BOX1 ).
478: 	 */
479: 	if(rx_data.phy_ch_hdr.ctrl & CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX)		/* rx ack. */
480: 	{
481: 		mb_phy_chnl_rx_ack_isr(&rx_data.phy_ch_ack);
482: 	}
483: 	else		/* rx cmd. */
484: 	{
485: 		mb_phy_chnl_rx_cmd_isr(&rx_data.phy_ch_cmd);
486: 	}
487: }

489: static void mb_phy_chnl_start_tx(u8 log_chnl)
490: {
491: 	u8		ret_code;
492: 
493: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx;
494: 
495: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
496: 
497: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
498: 
499: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // transferred to self.
500: 		return;
501: 
502: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
503: 		return;
504: 
505: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
506: 
507: 	if(phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state == CHNL_STATE_IDLE)
508: 	{
509: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state = CHNL_STATE_BUSY;		/* MUST set channel state to BUSY firstly. */
510: 		phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = rtos_get_time();
511: 		/* start_tx->tx_cmd->tx_isr callback->mb_chnl_write->start_tx, it is a loop.
512: 		   break the loop by setting the phy_chnl_cb.tx_state to busy. */
513: 
514: 		ret_code = mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd(log_chnl);
515: 
516: 		if(ret_code != 0)
517: 		{
518: 			/* tx_cmd failed before the data hit hardware: roll back BOTH
519: 			 * physical and logical state, so the caller can retry and so
520: 			 * the logical channel does not stay BUSY forever. */
521: 			u8                   log_chnl_idx_fail = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
522: 			mb_log_chnl_cb_t    *log_chnl_cb_x_fail =
523: 				(mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
524: 
525: 			if (log_chnl_idx_fail < phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx]) {
526: 				log_chnl_cb_x_fail[log_chnl_idx_fail].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
527: 			}
528: 			phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
529: 			phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = 0;
530: 		}
531: 	}
532: 
533: 	return;
534: }

536: volatile uint32_t s_mailbox_sync_cnt = 0;
537: 
538: static bk_err_t mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd_sync(u8 log_chnl, mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t *cmd_ptr)
539: {
540: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;
541: 	u16 			chnl_type;
542: 
543: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx;
544: 
545: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
546: 
547: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
548: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
549: 
550: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // transferred to self.
551: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
552: 
553: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
554: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
555: 
556: 	mailbox_endpoint_t    dst_cpu = (mailbox_endpoint_t)(phy_chnl_idx);
557: 
558: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = log_chnl;
559: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.tx_seq = 0;
560: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl  = CHNL_CTRL_SYNC_TX;
561: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.state = 0;
562: 
563: 	chnl_type = MB_PHY_CMD_CHNL;
564: 
565: 	s_mailbox_sync_cnt++;
566: 
567: 	/*
568: 	 * can't wait 'phy_chnl_cb.tx_state' to be CHNL_STATE_IDLE here,
569: 	 * 'phy_chnl_cb.tx_state' is set to CHNL_STATE_IDLE in interrupt callback.
570: 	 * but the interrupt may be disabled when this API is called.
571: 	 *    wait physical channel HW to be IDLE by <POLLing> !!
572: 	 */
573: 	while(1)
574: 	{
575: 		ret_code = bk_mailbox_send_safe((mailbox_data_t *)cmd_ptr, SELF_CPU, dst_cpu, (void *)&chnl_type);
576: 
577: 		if(ret_code != BK_ERR_MAILBOX_TIMEOUT)
578: 		{
579: 			break;
580: 		}
581: 	}
582: 
583: 	return ret_code;
584: }

586: static bk_err_t mb_phy_chnl_reset(u8 dst_cpu)
587: {
588: 	u16 				chnl_type;
589: 	mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t	cmd_buf = {0};
590: 
591: 	if(SELF_CPU == dst_cpu)
592: 	{
593: 		return BK_OK;
594: 	}
595: 
596: 	chnl_type = MB_PHY_ACK_CHNL;
597: 
598: 	cmd_buf.hdr.data = 0;
599: 	cmd_buf.hdr.ctrl |= (CHNL_CTRL_RESET | CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX);
600: 	cmd_buf.hdr.logical_chnl = CPX_LOG_CHNL_START(dst_cpu, SELF_CPU);
601: 
602: 	bk_mailbox_send_safe((mailbox_data_t *)&cmd_buf, SELF_CPU, dst_cpu, (void *)&chnl_type);
603: 
604: 	return BK_OK;
605: }

607: /* =====================      logical channel APIs      ==================*/
608: /*
609:   * init logical chnanel module.
610:   * return:
611:   *     succeed: BK_OK;
612:   *     failed  : fail code.
613:   *
614:   */
615: bk_err_t mb_chnl_init(void)
616: {
617: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;
618: 	int				i, j;
619: 
620: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
621: 
622: 	/*
623: 	 * mb_chnl_init() is reached from mb_chnl_open(), which is called by
624: 	 * many subsystems (shell log forwarding, ipc_init, mb_uart, ...).
625: 	 * Each one of those callers runs on its own FreeRTOS task and they
626: 	 * can race here:
627: 	 *
628: 	 *   Task A: enters mb_chnl_open(MB_CHNL_LOG), sees mb_chnnl_init_ok==0,
629: 	 *           enters mb_chnl_init(), runs all the memset's, sets
630: 	 *           mb_chnnl_init_ok=1, returns. Caller then sets
631: 	 *           log_chnl_cb2[15].in_used=1 and installs rx_isr.
632: 	 *   Task B (preempted in the middle of mb_chnl_open before the
633: 	 *           init_ok check finishes): comes back, sees init_ok still
634: 	 *           == 0 (because it sampled before A set it), enters
635: 	 *           mb_chnl_init() AGAIN, and the memset wipes the
636: 	 *           log_chnl_cb_x[] array that A just populated.
637: 	 *
638: 	 * Fix: serialize the body with the existing critical section so the
639: 	 * "if (init_ok) return; ... init_ok = 1;" sequence is atomic w.r.t.
640: 	 * other tasks. The double-check pattern still keeps the fast path
641: 	 * lock-free once init has completed.
642: 	 */
643: 	if(mb_chnnl_init_ok)
644: 	{
645: 		return BK_OK;
646: 	}
647: 
648: 	uint32_t init_int_mask = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
649: 	if(mb_chnnl_init_ok)
650: 	{
651: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(init_int_mask);
652: 		return BK_OK;
653: 	}
654: 
655: 	memset(&phy_chnl_x_cb, 0, sizeof(phy_chnl_x_cb));
656: 	for(i = 0; i < PHY_CHNL_NUM; i++)
657: 	{
658: 		phy_chnl_x_cb[i].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
659: 
660: 		log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[i]);
661: 
662: 		memset(log_chnl_cb_x, 0, sizeof(mb_log_chnl_cb_t) * phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[i]);
663: 
664: 		for(j = 0; j < phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[i]; j++)
665: 		{
666: 			log_chnl_cb_x[j].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
667: 		}
668: 	}
669: 
670: 	ret_code = bk_mailbox_init();
671: 	if(ret_code != BK_OK)
672: 	{
673: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(init_int_mask);
674: 		return ret_code;
675: 	}
676: 
677: 	mailbox_endpoint_t    dst_cpu;
678: 
679: 	for(i = 0; i < PHY_CHNL_NUM; i++)
680: 	{
681: 		dst_cpu = (mailbox_endpoint_t)(i);  // dst_cpu_id;
682: 
683: 		bk_mailbox_recv_callback_register(dst_cpu, SELF_CPU, mb_phy_chnl_rx_isr);
684: 	}
685: 
686: 	mb_phy_chnl_reset(0);
687: 
688: 	mb_chnnl_init_ok = 1;
689: 
690: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(init_int_mask);
691: 
692: 	return BK_OK;
693: }

695: /*
696:   * open logical chnanel.
697:   * input:

705: bk_err_t mb_chnl_open(u8 log_chnl, void * callback_param)

711: 		ret_code = mb_chnl_init();
712: 
713: 		if(ret_code != BK_OK)

715: 			return ret_code;
716: 		}
717: 	}
718: 
719: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
720: 	u8		log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
721: 
722: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
723: 
724: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
725: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
726: 
727: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // transferred to self.
728: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
729: 
730: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
731: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
732: 
733: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);

735: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])

744: 	return BK_OK;

801: /*
802:   * write to logical chnanel.
803:   * input:
804:   *     log_chnl     : logical channel id to write.
805:   *     cmd_buf     : buffer of channel cmd data.
806:   * return:
807:   *     succeed: BK_OK;
808:   *     failed  : fail code.
809:   *
810:   */
811: bk_err_t mb_chnl_write(u8 log_chnl, mb_chnl_cmd_t * cmd_buf)
812: {
813: 	u16		write_len;
814: 
815: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
816: 	u8		log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
817: 
818: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
819: 
820: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
821: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
822: 
823: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // transferred to self.
824: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
825: 
826: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
827: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
828: 
829: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
830: 
831: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
832: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
833: 
834: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].in_used == 0)
835: 		return BK_ERR_STATE;
836: 
837: 	u32 int_mask = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
838: 
839: 	/* If the physical channel has been BUSY abnormally long (peer never
840: 	 * sent ACK / lost interrupt / lost ack), forcibly recover it so this
841: 	 * and all future mb_chnl_write() calls on the channel don't deadlock. */
842: 	{
843: 		mb_phy_chnl_cb_t *phy_cb_chk = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
844: 
845: 		if ((phy_cb_chk->tx_state == CHNL_STATE_BUSY) && (phy_cb_chk->busy_since_ms != 0))
846: 		{
847: 			u32 now = rtos_get_time();
848: 			u32 age = now - phy_cb_chk->busy_since_ms;	/* unsigned wrap is fine for short windows */
849: 
850: 			if (age >= MB_PHY_CHNL_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS)
851: 			{
852: 				phy_cb_chk->tx_fault_cnt++;
853: 				phy_cb_chk->tx_fault_cnt |= 0x20000000;	/* mark "BUSY-stuck recovered" */
854: 				phy_cb_chk->tx_state      = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
855: 				phy_cb_chk->busy_since_ms = 0;
856: 			}
857: 		}
858: 	}
859: 
860: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state != CHNL_STATE_IDLE)
861: 	{
862: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
863: 
864: 		return BK_ERR_BUSY;
865: 	}
866: 
867: 	write_len = sizeof(mailbox_data_t) > sizeof(mb_chnl_cmd_t) ? sizeof(mb_chnl_cmd_t) : sizeof(mailbox_data_t);
868: 
869: 	memcpy(&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff, cmd_buf, write_len);
870: 
871: 	/* set to BUSY means there is data in tx-buff. mb_phy_chnl_rx_ack_isr will get it to send. */
872: 	log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_BUSY;   /* MUST set to BUSY after data was copied. */
873: 	__DMB();
874: 
875: 	mb_phy_chnl_start_tx(log_chnl);
876: 
877: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
878: 
879: 	return BK_OK;
880: }

919: 	switch(cmd)

921: 		case MB_CHNL_GET_STATUS:
922: 
923: 			if(param == NULL)
924: 				return BK_ERR_NULL_PARAM;

926: 			*((u8 *)param) = log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state;

928: 			break;

932: 			break;

35: static void mbox0_drv_isr_handler(void)
36: {
37: 	uint32_t int_status;
38: 	uint32_t fifo_status;
39: 	mbox0_message_t message;
40: 
41: 	int_status = mbox0_dev.chn_drv[SELF_CHNL]->chn_get_int_status(&mbox0_dev.hal);
42: 
43: 	if(int_status == 0)
44: 		return;
45: 
46: 	do
47: 	{
48: 		fifo_status = mbox0_dev.chn_drv[SELF_CHNL]->chn_get_rx_fifo_stat(&mbox0_dev.hal);
49: 		
50: 		if(fifo_status & RX_FIFO_STAT_NOT_EMPTY)
51: 		{
52: 			mbox0_drv_recieve_message(&message);
53: 
54: 			if(message.data[1] != 0)  /* message data len is not 0. */
55: 			{
56: 				if(mbox0_dev.rx_callback != NULL)
57: 					mbox0_dev.rx_callback(&message);
58: 			}
59: 			else
60: 			{
61: 				#if CONFIG_SOC_SMP
62: 				extern void crosscore_smp_cmd_handler(uint8_t src_core, uint32_t cmd);
63: 				
64: 				crosscore_smp_cmd_handler(message.src_cpu, message.data[0]);
65: 				#endif
66: 			}
67: 		}
68: 		else
69: 		{
70: 			break;
71: 		}

# BK7258 AP mailbox v2 to NuttX CPU1 transport specification

## 1. Scope and conclusion

The BK7258 AP/CP PWC path does not use the older `s_mailbox_t` two-box peripheral directly. The active PWC implementation uses the BK7258 mailbox v2 block, called `mbox0` in the source tree:

- Hardware: `SOC_MBOX0_REG_BASE`, mailbox v2 register block.
- Physical channels: three hardware FIFO channels, selected by the local CPU/core.
- Transport payload: a two-word hardware FIFO entry containing:
  1. a pointer to a four-word shared-memory payload;
  2. the payload length.
- Logical transport protocol: the `mailbox_channel.c` protocol layered above the FIFO.
- PWC logical channel:
  - AP/CPU1 → CP/CPU0: logical channel `MB_CHNL_PWC = 0x12`.
  - CP/CPU0 → AP/CPU1: logical channel `MB_CHNL_PWC = 0x42`.
- The mailbox-channel layer adds the actual command/ACK header, sequence number, logical channel ID, ACK-box marker, and physical-channel state.

For a minimal but protocol-compatible NuttX CPU1 implementation, the essential boot-ready path is:

1. Configure the BK7258 mailbox v2 channel-1 FIFO for CPU1 reception/transmission.
2. Register and enable the mailbox interrupt for CPU1.
3. Use a pair of cache-visible, shared four-word payload buffers per destination or otherwise guarantee that a payload remains valid until consumed.
4. Encode the physical message as `{shared_buffer_pointer, 16}`.
5. Implement the logical-channel command format and ACK format.
6. Use logical channel `0x12` for CPU1/AP PWC traffic to CPU0/CP.
7. Open/register PWC before sending `PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD`.
8. Process incoming PWC commands in the CPU1 IRQ callback and issue protocol ACKs.
9. Preserve the sequence and channel-state rules, including one outstanding physical transaction per destination and ACK matching.

The older mailbox block under `ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/mailbox_struct.h` is not the PWC transport used by the current AP/CP implementation. It is a separate two-box register abstraction and should not be used for the NuttX CPU1 PWC path unless the surrounding firmware is deliberately changed.

---

# 2. Source tree and active implementation

## 2.1 AP implementation

Relevant AP files:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/mbox0_struct.h`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/mbox0_ll.h`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/common/hal/mbox0_hal.c`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.c`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c`

The AP build includes the v2 driver and logical-channel layer at:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/CMakeLists.txt:434-446`

The relevant source entries include:

- `mailbox/mbox0_drv.c`
- `mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c`
- `mailbox/mbox0_cross_core.c`
- `mailbox/mailbox_channel.c`

## 2.2 CP counterpart

Relevant CP files:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/soc/mbox0_struct.h`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/hal/mbox0_ll.h`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/mbox0_hal.c`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.c`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c`

The AP and CP v2 mailbox drivers are substantially identical. Their local CPU identity and physical-channel selection differ.

---

# 3. Hardware mailbox v2 register layout

## 3.1 Base address

BK7258 mailbox v2 base addresses are defined in:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/soc/bk7258/reg_base.h:72-73`

```c
#define SOC_MBOX0_REG_BASE       (0x41000000 + SOC_ADDR_OFFSET)
#define SOC_MBOX1_REG_BASE       (0x41020000 + SOC_ADDR_OFFSET)
```

The active `mbox0` block uses:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/mailbox_reg.h:23-25`

```c
#define MAILBOX_BASE (SOC_MBOX0_REG_BASE)
```

The v2 low-level driver then defines:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/mbox0_ll.h:25-26`

```c
#define MBOX0_FIFO_SIZE 8
#define MBOX0_LL_REG_BASE (MAILBOX_BASE)
```

The CP counterpart uses the corresponding CP BK7258 base definitions and the same v2 register layout.

## 3.2 Exact hardware register struct

The exact AP register struct is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/mbox0_struct.h:23-655`

The struct is:

```c
typedef volatile struct {
    /* 0x00 */
    union {
        struct {
            volatile uint32_t DeviceID : 32;
        };
        uint32_t v;
    } reg_0x0;

    /* 0x04 */
    union {
        struct {
            volatile uint32_t VersionID : 32;
        };
        uint32_t v;
    } reg_0x1;

    /* 0x08 */
    union {
        struct {
            volatile uint32_t softrstn          : 1; /* bit 0 */
            volatile uint32_t hclk_bps          : 1; /* bit 1 */
            volatile uint32_t chn_pro_disable   : 1; /* bit 2 */
            volatile uint32_t reserved3         : 29;
        };
        uint32_t v;
    } reg_0x2;

    /* 0x0c */
    union {
        struct {
            volatile uint32_t int_status_chn0 : 1; /* bit 0 */
            volatile uint32_t int_status_chn1 : 1; /* bit 1 */
            volatile uint32_t int_status_chn2 : 1; /* bit 2 */
            volatile uint32_t reserved3       : 29;
        };
        uint32_t v;
    } reg_0x3;

    /* 0x10 through 0x3c: channel registers */
} mbox0_hw_t;
```

The exact generated members for channels 0, 1, and 2 are described below.

## 3.3 Channel register blocks

Each hardware channel occupies 0x40 bytes / 16 registers.

### Channel 0

Offsets:

| Register | Offset | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| `reg_0x10` | `0x40` | FIFO start, interrupt enables/status, non-empty |
| `reg_0x11` | `0x44` | channel enable and FIFO length |
| `reg_0x12` | `0x48` | transmit data word 0 |
| `reg_0x13` | `0x4c` | transmit data word 1 |
| `reg_0x14` | `0x50` | destination CPU/TID; writing starts transmission |
| `reg_0x15` | `0x54` | source CPU/SID; reading starts reception |
| `reg_0x16` | `0x58` | receive data word 0 |
| `reg_0x17` | `0x5c` | receive data word 1 |
| `reg_0x18` | `0x60` | FIFO full/empty/count |

Evidence:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/mbox0_struct.h:191-297`

### Channel 1

Offsets:

| Register | Offset | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| `reg_0x20` | `0x80` | FIFO start, interrupt enables/status, non-empty |
| `reg_0x21` | `0x84` | channel enable and FIFO length |
| `reg_0x22` | `0x88` | transmit data word 0 |
| `reg_0x23` | `0x8c` | transmit data word 1 |
| `reg_0x24` | `0x90` | destination CPU/TID; writing starts transmission |
| `reg_0x25` | `0x94` | source CPU/SID; reading starts reception |
| `reg_0x26` | `0x98` | receive data word 0 |
| `reg_0x27` | `0x9c` | receive data word 1 |
| `reg_0x28` | `0xa0` | FIFO full/empty/count |

Evidence:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/mbox0_struct.h:369-475`

### Channel 2

Offsets:

| Register | Offset | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| `reg_0x30` | `0xc0` | FIFO start, interrupt enables/status, non-empty |
| `reg_0x31` | `0xc4` | channel enable and FIFO length |
| `reg_0x32` | `0xc8` | transmit data word 0 |
| `reg_0x33` | `0xcc` | transmit data word 1 |
| `reg_0x34` | `0xd0` | destination CPU/TID; writing starts transmission |
| `reg_0x35` | `0xd4` | source CPU/SID; reading starts reception |

Evidence:

The full hardware struct is 0xE4 bytes in register terms, ending at register `0x38`.

---

# 4. Register field semantics

## 4.1 Global control register `reg_0x2`

Fields are defined at:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/mbox0_struct.h:45-56`

| Bit | Field | Required behavior |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | `softrstn` | Set to 1 during device initialization |
| 1 | `hclk_bps` | Set to 0 |
| 2 | `chn_pro_disable` | Set to 1 by CPU0 during FIFO setup, allowing software to configure all channels |

The AP HAL initialization sequence is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/common/hal/mbox0_hal.c:432-444`

```c
mbox0_ll_set_reg_0x2_softrstn(hw, 1);
mbox0_ll_set_reg_0x2_hclk_bps(hw, 0);
mbox0_ll_set_reg_0x2_chn_pro_disable(hw, 0);
```

Then the driver specifically unprotects channels:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.c:109-115`

```c
mbox0_hal_dev_init(&mbox0_dev.hal);
mbox0_hal_set_reg_0x2_chn_pro_disable(&mbox0_dev.hal, 1);

for (...) {
    chn_cfg_fifo(...);
}
```

The distinction is important:

- `mbox0_hal_dev_init()` initially sets `chn_pro_disable = 0`.
- The driver then sets it to `1` before configuring FIFO ownership.

A minimal boot-ready implementation should reproduce both operations in the same order unless the NuttX platform initialization already performs them.

## 4.2 Global interrupt status `reg_0x3`

Fields:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/mbox0_struct.h:58-69`

```c
bit 0: int_status_chn0
bit 1: int_status_chn1
bit 2: int_status_chn2
```

The channel driver reads this register and extracts the local channel bit:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/common/hal/mbox0_hal.c:199-244`

- channel 0: bit 0
- channel 1: bit 1
- channel 2: bit 2

## 4.3 Per-channel FIFO control register

For channel 1, `reg_0x20` contains:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/mbox0_struct.h:369-388`

| Bits | Field |
|---:|---|
| 5:0 | `fifo_start` |
| 8 | `int_en` |
| 9 | `int_wrerr_en` |
| 10 | `int_rderr_en` |
| 11 | `int_wrfull_en` |
| 16 | `wrerr_int_sta`, write-1-to-clear |
| 17 | `rderr_int_sta`, write-1-to-clear |

- `reg_0x26`: receive data word 0.
- `reg_0x27`: receive data word 1.

# 5. Exact mbox0 software structures

## 5.1 Hardware FIFO message

Defined by:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/common/hal/include/mbox0_hal.h:52-67`

```c
typedef struct
{
    union
    {
        uint8_t src_cpu;
        uint8_t dest_cpu;
    };
    uint32_t data[2];
} mbox0_message_t;
```

Logical layout:

| Offset | Size | Meaning |
|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | 1 | source CPU on receive, destination CPU on transmit |
| 1-3 | 3 | union padding |
| 4 | 4 | hardware FIFO word 0 |
| 8 | 4 | hardware FIFO word 1 |

`sizeof(mbox0_message_t)` should be 12 bytes on the target ABI, although only the fields are transferred to hardware; the hardware FIFO entry itself is two 32-bit words plus the TID supplied through the register interface.

For protocol compatibility, the actual FIFO payload is:

```text
FIFO word 0 = shared payload address
FIFO word 1 = sizeof(mailbox_data_t) = 16
destination = CPU ID
```

## 5.2 Shared payload

The public mailbox payload is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_types.h:64-70`

```c
typedef struct
{
    uint32_t param0;
    uint32_t param1;
    uint32_t param2;
    uint32_t param3;
} mailbox_data_t;
```

The size is exactly 16 bytes.

The adapter allocates:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c:11-13`

```c
static mailbox_data_t mailbox_buff[MBOX_CHNL_NUM][TX_BOX_NUM];
static mailbox_callback_t mailbox_callback[MBOX_CHNL_NUM] = {0};
static uint8_t mailbox_tx_box[MBOX_CHNL_NUM] = {0};
```

with:

```c
TX_CMD_BOX = 0;
TX_ACK_BOX = 1;
TX_BOX_NUM = 2;
```

Thus, the reference implementation reserves two 16-byte buffers per destination CPU:

```text
mailbox_buff[3][2]
```

For CPU1-only NuttX support, the minimum practical equivalent is:

```c
#define MBOX0_SHARED_SLOTS 2

static volatile struct mailbox_data_s {
    uint32_t param0;
    uint32_t param1;
    uint32_t param2;
    uint32_t param3;
} cpu1_tx_shared[MBOX0_SHARED_SLOTS];
```

However, the buffer must satisfy all of the following:

1. It is visible to both CPUs.
2. It is in a mutually accessible memory region.
3. It is not reclaimed or overwritten until the remote CPU has consumed the FIFO entry and copied the pointed-to payload.
4. It is cache-coherent, or explicit cache maintenance is used.
5. The pointer value fits in the 32-bit hardware word.

The adapter writes the buffer before sending:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c:113-123`

```c
mailbox_tx_box[dst] = (mailbox_tx_box[dst] + 1) % TX_BOX_NUM;
box = mailbox_tx_box[dst];

memcpy(&mailbox_buff[dst][box], data, sizeof(mailbox_data_t));

message.data[0] = (u32)(&mailbox_buff[dst][box]);
message.data[1] = sizeof(mailbox_data_t);
message.dest_cpu = (uint8_t)dst;
```

The CP adapter is identical:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c:113-123`

## 5.3 Receive-side shared-buffer handling

The receiving adapter validates the length:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c:15-38`

```c
if (msg->data[1] == sizeof(data))
{
#if CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLE
    extern void flush_dcache(void *va, long size);
    flush_dcache((void *)msg->data[0], sizeof(data));
#endif
    memcpy(&data, (u8 *)msg->data[0], sizeof(data));
}
else
{
    return;
}
```

Required NuttX behavior:

```text
if fifo_word1 != 16:
    discard the message

if cache is not coherent:
    invalidate/flush the pointed-to 16-byte shared buffer before copying

copy exactly 16 bytes into a local mailbox_data_t

only then invoke the protocol callback
```

The callback receives a local copy, not the shared pointer:

```c
mailbox_callback[chnl](&data);
```

That means the shared payload does not need to remain valid after the adapter's receive callback has copied it.

## 6.1 FIFO capacity

The v2 block has eight FIFO entries total:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/mbox0_ll.h:25-35`


## 6.2 AP/SMP partition

The AP/CPU1 side configures:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.c:6-27`

```c
#define MBOX0_CHN0_FIFO_LEN 2
#define MBOX0_CHN1_FIFO_LEN 3
#define MBOX0_CHN2_FIFO_LEN 3

#define MBOX0_CHN0_FIFO_START 0
```

Therefore:

| Hardware channel | FIFO start | FIFO length | AP/SMP role |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | 0 | 2 | CPU0/core0 channel |
| 1 | 2 | 3 | CPU1 channel |
| 2 | 5 | 3 | CPU2 channel |

The AP driver chooses the local channel with:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.h:26-29`

```c
#if CONFIG_SOC_SMP
#define SELF_CHNL rtos_get_core_id()
#else
#define SELF_CHNL 1
#endif
```

For the NuttX CPU1 target, `SELF_CHNL` must therefore resolve to hardware channel 1.

## 6.3 CP partition

The CP counterpart uses the same FIFO partition:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.c:7-22`

```c
#define MBOX0_CHN0_FIFO_LEN 2
#define MBOX0_CHN1_FIFO_LEN 3
#define MBOX0_CHN2_FIFO_LEN 3
```

The CP non-SMP local channel is CPU0:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.h:26-30`

```c
#if CONFIG_SOC_SMP
#define SELF_CHNL rtos_get_core_id()
#else
#define SELF_CHNL 0
#endif
```

Consequently:

```text
CP CPU0 uses hardware channel 0.
AP CPU1 uses hardware channel 1.
```

This channel pairing is essential. A CPU1 implementation using channel 0 will not be compatible with the existing CP0 path.

# 7. Physical hardware send and receive sequence

## 7.1 Send sequence

The hardware send sequence is:

1. Confirm destination FIFO is not full.
2. Copy the 16-byte payload into a shared slot.
3. Place shared-slot address in a local message word.
4. Place length 16 in the second local message word.
5. Write `mail_tdata0`.
6. Write `mail_tdata1`.
7. Write `mail_tid = destination CPU`.
8. The `mail_tid` write starts the transfer.

Evidence:

- FIFO check: `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c:99-110`
- slot rotation and shared copy: lines 113-120
- destination and send: lines 121-123
- channel-1 register writes: `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/common/hal/mbox0_hal.c:69-80`

The adapter returns:

- `BK_ERR_MAILBOX_TIMEOUT` if destination FIFO is full.
- `BK_ERR_MAILBOX_SRC_DST` on invalid destination or status failure.
- `BK_ERR_MAILBOX_NOT_INIT` if the low-level send fails.

A NuttX implementation should preserve these distinctions at least internally, even if it maps them to `-EBUSY`, `-EINVAL`, and `-EIO`.

## 7.2 Receive IRQ sequence

The low-level IRQ handler:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.c:40-79`

does the following:

1. Read the local channel interrupt status.
2. Return if no interrupt is asserted.
3. Repeatedly:
   - read RX FIFO status;
   - if not empty, read one message;
   - if `data[1] != 0`, dispatch the mailbox callback;
   - otherwise treat it as an SMP cross-core command;
   - stop when FIFO is empty.

For CPU1, the IRQ must read channel 1's:

- interrupt status bit: global `reg_0x3[1]`;
- FIFO status: channel-1 `reg_0x28`;
- source ID/data:
  - `reg_0x25.mail_sid`
  - `reg_0x26.mail_rdata0`
  - `reg_0x27.mail_rdata1`

The IRQ must drain the FIFO completely, not process only one entry. This is required because the hardware FIFO depth is three for channel 1 and multiple logical-channel messages may arrive before the interrupt is serviced.

## 7.3 Interrupt enable sequence

The driver registers the ISR:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.c:158-163`

```c
bk_int_isr_register(INT_SRC_MAILBOX, mbox0_drv_isr_handler, NULL);
```

Then it initializes each local core/channel and enables the hardware/system interrupt:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.c:118-142`

```c
chn_int_enable(..., 1);
drain RX FIFO;
sys_drv_core_intr_group2_enable(
    id,
    (1 << (int_src - 32))
);
```

For the NuttX CPU1 port, the equivalent ordering should be:

```text
1. map mailbox v2 registers;
2. reset/enable mailbox block;
3. configure FIFO layout;
4. configure CPU1 channel 1 interrupt enable;
5. drain stale channel-1 RX FIFO;
6. register the NuttX IRQ handler;
7. enable the CPU1 system interrupt route;
8. initialize logical-channel state;
9. open PWC;
10. install PWC receive/complete callbacks;
11. send CPU1 boot-ready notification.
```

Do not enable the CPU1 mailbox interrupt before the handler and shared protocol state are ready.

# 8. Logical-channel protocol

## 8.1 CPU routing bits

The logical channel format is defined in:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:32-44`

```c
#define DST_CPU_ID_MASK 0xC0
#define DST_CPU_ID_POS  6

#define SRC_CPU_ID_MASK 0x30
#define SRC_CPU_ID_POS  4

#define LOG_CHNL_ID_MASK 0x0F

#define GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl) \
    (((log_chnl) & SRC_CPU_ID_MASK) >> SRC_CPU_ID_POS)

#define GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl) \
    (((log_chnl) & DST_CPU_ID_MASK) >> DST_CPU_ID_POS)

#define CPX_LOG_CHNL_START(src_cpu, dst_cpu) \
    ((((dst_cpu) << DST_CPU_ID_POS) & DST_CPU_ID_MASK) + \
     (((src_cpu) << SRC_CPU_ID_POS) & SRC_CPU_ID_MASK))

#define GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl) \
    ((log_chnl) & LOG_CHNL_ID_MASK)
```

The logical channel byte is:

```text
bits 7:6 = destination CPU ID
bits 5:4 = source CPU ID
bits 3:0 = logical channel index
```

## 8.2 PWC logical channel IDs

AP/CPU1 source and CPU0 destination are defined at:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:53-99`

```c
#define SELF_CPU MAILBOX_CPU1

#define CP0_MB_LOG_CHNL_START CPX_LOG_CHNL_START(SELF_CPU, MAILBOX_CPU0)

#define MB_CHNL_HW_CTRL CP0_MB_LOG_CHNL_START
#define CP0_MB_CHNL_IPC
#define MB_CHNL_PWC
```

Calculation:

```text
src = 1
dst = 0

CPX_LOG_CHNL_START(1, 0)
    = (0 << 6) | (1 << 4)
    = 0x10

MB_CHNL_HW_CTRL = 0x10
CP0_MB_CHNL_IPC = 0x11
MB_CHNL_PWC     = 0x12
```

CP/CPU0 source and CPU1 destination are defined at:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:49-86`

```c
#define SELF_CPU MAILBOX_CPU0

#define CP1_MB_LOG_CHNL_START CPX_LOG_CHNL_START(SELF_CPU, MAILBOX_CPU1)

#define MB_CHNL_HW_CTRL CP1_MB_LOG_CHNL_START
#define CP1_MB_CHNL_IPC
#define MB_CHNL_PWC
```

Calculation:

```text
src = 0
dst = 1

CPX_LOG_CHNL_START(0, 1)
    = (1 << 6) | (0 << 4)
    = 0x40

MB_CHNL_HW_CTRL = 0x40
CP1_MB_CHNL_IPC = 0x41
MB_CHNL_PWC     = 0x42
```

Important: the symbolic name `MB_CHNL_PWC` is `0x12` on AP/CPU1 and `0x42` on CP/CPU0. The same name is direction-local.

## 8.3 Command header

Defined in:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:106-127`

```c
#define CHNL_STATE_MASK 0xF
#define CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL 0x1

typedef union
{
    struct
    {
        u32 cmd      : 8;
        u32 state    : 4;
        u32 Reserved : 20;
    };
    u32 data;
} mb_chnl_hdr_t;

typedef struct
{
    mb_chnl_hdr_t hdr;
    u32 param1;
    u32 param2;
    u32 param3;
} mb_chnl_cmd_t;
```

Exact wire payload for a normal logical command:

```text
param0 = header.data
param1 = command parameter 1
param2 = command parameter 2
param3 = command parameter 3
```

The four 32-bit words are:

```text
word 0:
    bits  7:0   command
    bits 11:8   command state
    bits 31:12  reserved, must be zero for normal commands

word 1: param1
word 2: param2
word 3: param3
```

The PWC producer sets only `hdr.cmd` and the three parameters:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:260-271`

```c
mb_chnl_cmd_t mb_cmd = {0};

mb_cmd.hdr.cmd = cmd;
mb_cmd.param1 = param1;
mb_cmd.param2 = param2;
mb_cmd.param3 = param3;

ret = mb_chnl_write(MB_CHNL_PWC, &mb_cmd);
```

## 8.4 ACK structure

Defined in:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:129-147`

```c
enum
{
    ACK_STATE_PENDING = 0x01,
    ACK_STATE_COMPLETE,
    ACK_STATE_FAIL,
};

typedef struct
{
    mb_chnl_hdr_t hdr;
    u32 ack_data1;
    u32 ack_data2;
    union
    {
        u32 ack_data3;
        u32 ack_state;
    };
} mb_chnl_ack_t;
```

Wire layout:

```text
word 0:
    cmd       = original command
    state     = ACK_STATE_PENDING, COMPLETE, or FAIL
    reserved  = zero or protocol-preserved bits

word 1: ack_data1
word 2: ack_data2
word 3: ack_data3 or ack_state
```

The RX callback receives a command buffer and then reuses the same four-word buffer as the ACK buffer:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:152-156`

> `rx_isr` first uses the buffer as the command buffer; after handling the command, it uses the buffer as an acknowledge buffer.

At the physical layer, the command is returned to the sender through the ACK box marker. See Section 9.

# 9. Physical logical-channel framing, ACK, and sequence state

The logical channel implementation is in:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c`

## 9.1 Physical header

The physical header is defined at lines 64-84:

```c
typedef union
{
    struct
    {
        u32 cmd          : 8;
        u32 state        : 4;
        u32 ctrl         : 4;
        u32 tx_seq       : 8;
        u32 logical_chnl : 8;
    };
    u32 data;
} phy_chnnl_hdr_t;

typedef struct
{
    phy_chnnl_hdr_t hdr;
    u32 param1;
    u32 param2;
    u32 param3;
} mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t;
```

The physical ACK has the same header and three data words:

```c
typedef struct
{
    phy_chnnl_hdr_t hdr;
    u32 data1;
    u32 data2;
    u32 data3;
} mb_phy_chnl_ack_t;
```

The first word layout is:

```text
bits  7:0   cmd
bits 11:8   state
bits 15:12  ctrl
bits 23:16  tx_seq
bits 31:24  logical_chnl
```

This physical header is what occupies `mailbox_data_t.param0` on the hardware wire.

## 9.2 Control bits

Defined at:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:52-62`

```c
#define CHNL_CTRL_MASK     0xF
#define CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX  0x01
#define CHNL_CTRL_SYNC_TX  0x02
#define CHNL_CTRL_RESET    0x04
```

Semantics:

| Bit | Name | Meaning |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | `CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX` | Physical ACK; receiver must route it to the ACK path |
| 1 | `CHNL_CTRL_SYNC_TX` | Synchronous command; receiver does not return an ACK |
| 2 | `CHNL_CTRL_RESET` | Reset/reinitialize peer physical-channel state |

The physical command and physical ACK are distinguished by bit 0 in the header, not by a separately visible hardware box ID. The implementation explicitly states:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:473-477`

> The current mailbox driver cannot identify which hardware box the message came from, so `CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX` distinguishes ACK traffic.

For the v2 mbox0 path, the hardware itself presents a FIFO channel rather than the older two-box mailbox abstraction. The logical protocol still retains this ACK-box marker for compatibility.

## 9.3 Physical command transmit sequence

`mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd()` is at:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:194-257`

Required sequence:

1. Validate source CPU equals local CPU.
2. Validate destination CPU is not local and is in range.
3. Increment the physical TX sequence.
4. Record the logical channel in the physical control block.
5. Copy the logical command into the per-logical-channel transmit buffer.
6. Set:
   - `logical_chnl = log_chnl`
   - `tx_seq = current sequence`
   - `ctrl = 0`
   - `state = 0`
7. Execute a data memory barrier.
8. Send the four-word payload to the destination CPU.
9. Mark the logical channel available for future queueing.
10. Invoke the logical TX callback, if any.

The sequence must be incremented before placing the command on the hardware FIFO.

## 9.4 Physical channel state

The physical control block is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:36-49`

```c
typedef struct
{
    volatile u8 tx_state;
    u8 tx_seq;
    u8 tx_log_chnl;
    u8 tx_hdr_cmd;
    u32 rx_fault_cnt;
    u32 tx_fault_cnt;
    volatile u32 busy_since_ms;
} mb_phy_chnl_cb_t;
```

A minimal NuttX implementation needs at least:

```c
struct cpu1_phy_state {
    volatile uint8_t tx_state;
    uint8_t tx_seq;
    uint8_t tx_log_chnl;
    uint8_t tx_hdr_cmd;
    uint32_t rx_fault_cnt;
    uint32_t tx_fault_cnt;
};
```

`busy_since_ms` and the 200 ms recovery watchdog are recommended but optional for first boot.

The reference state values are:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:26-34`

```c
#define CHNL_STATE_BUSY 1
#define CHNL_STATE_IDLE 0
#define MB_PHY_CHNL_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS 200
```

Physical state transition:

```text
IDLE
  -> BUSY before first hardware send
  -> remains BUSY until matching ACK
  -> IDLE after matching ACK
```

The state must be set to BUSY before the send routine is called. The source explicitly emphasizes this:

`mailbox_channel.c:505-514`

> MUST set channel state to BUSY firstly.

Only one physical transaction is active for a given destination CPU. Logical channels queue behind the physical channel.

## 9.5 Receiving a command

The physical command receive path is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:376-459`

Required steps:

1. Extract `logical_chnl` from the physical header.
2. Interpret the source CPU from the logical channel.
3. Interpret the destination CPU from the logical channel.
4. Validate that the destination is the local CPU.
5. Validate source CPU and logical channel index.
6. Preserve a copy of the original physical header.
7. Clear non-command physical header fields before invoking the logical callback:
   - logical channel
   - sequence
   - control
   - state
8. Call the registered logical RX callback.
9. The callback modifies the same four-word buffer into ACK data.
10. If the command was synchronous, do not ACK.
11. Otherwise:
    - restore the saved physical header;
    - set `CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX`;
    - send the same four-word buffer back to the source CPU.

The callback's command header remains in the ACK:

`mailbox_channel.c:329-335`

For a received ACK, the implementation clears:

- `logical_chnl`
- `tx_seq`
- `ctrl`

but preserves:

- `cmd`
- `state`

before invoking the logical TX-complete callback.

## 9.6 Receiving an ACK

The ACK receive path is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:259-374`

The ACK is accepted only if:

```text
ack.logical_chnl == outstanding.tx_log_chnl
ack.tx_seq       == outstanding.tx_seq
```

Evidence:

`mailbox_channel.c:291-294`

A mismatched ACK is stale or corrupt and must not complete the transaction.

The current source additionally recovers the physical channel on mismatch:

`mailbox_channel.c:297-323`

A minimal boot implementation may initially count and discard mismatched ACKs, but a production implementation should also release the stuck physical channel and dispatch queued logical messages as the reference does.

On a matching ACK:

1. Clear the physical framing fields before callback:
   - `logical_chnl = 0`
   - `tx_seq = 0`
   - `ctrl = 0`
2. Preserve `cmd` and `state`.
3. Call the registered TX-complete callback.
4. Search logical channels in priority order.
5. Send the next pending logical message.
6. If no logical message is pending, mark physical state IDLE.

The logical-channel search is ascending by logical index:

`mailbox_channel.c:340-355`

Because the lower logical channel number has higher priority, PWC (`index 2`) has higher priority than later channels such as Wi-Fi data or logging.

# 13. CPU1 initialization sequence

## 13.1 Required boot-ready sequence

The recommended NuttX CPU1 initialization sequence is:

### Step 1: Map hardware

Map:

```text
MBOX0 base = 0x41000000 + SOC_ADDR_OFFSET
CPU1 channel block = channel 1
```

For direct register access, use channel-1 offsets:

```text
reg_0x20 = base + 0x80
reg_0x21 = base + 0x84
reg_0x22 = base + 0x88
reg_0x23 = base + 0x8c
reg_0x24 = base + 0x90
reg_0x25 = base + 0x94
reg_0x26 = base + 0x98
reg_0x27 = base + 0x9c
reg_0x28 = base + 0xa0
```

### Step 2: Initialize/reset the block

Set:

```text
reg_0x2.softrstn = 1
reg_0x2.hclk_bps = 0
```

If CPU0 owns global FIFO configuration, do not rewrite the global configuration from CPU1. Otherwise, set:

```text
reg_0x2.chn_pro_disable = 1
```

before configuring channel 1.

### Step 3: Configure FIFO partition

The partition must match CP:

```text
channel 0: start 0, length 2
channel 1: start 2, length 3
channel 2: start 5, length 3
```

For CPU1 channel 1:

```text
reg_0x20.fifo_start = 2
reg_0x21.fifo_length = 3
reg_0x21.chn_enable = 1
```

Write the start address before enabling the channel.

### Step 4: Configure normal interrupt

For channel 1:

```text
reg_0x20.int_wrerr_en  = 0
reg_0x20.int_rderr_en  = 0
reg_0x20.int_wrfull_en = 0
reg_0x20.int_en        = 1
```

### Step 5: Drain stale RX FIFO

While:

```text
reg_0x28.fifo_empt == 0
```

read:

```text
reg_0x25.mail_sid
reg_0x26.mail_rdata0
reg_0x27.mail_rdata1
```

Discard stale messages before registering PWC state.

### Step 6: Register IRQ

Register the CPU1 mailbox IRQ and make it drain channel 1 until `fifo_empt == 1`.

The AP mbox0 driver registers the logical mailbox ISR using `INT_SRC_MAILBOX`:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.c:158-163`

The system interrupt source definitions include mailbox entries at:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/int_types.h:70-72`

```c
INT_SRC_MAILBOX0,
INT_SRC_MAILBOX1,
```

The CPU1 NuttX port must use the interrupt line routed to CPU1's channel-1 mailbox receive path, not the legacy `IRQ_MAILBOX1` definition associated with the older mailbox block unless the SoC interrupt controller explicitly maps them together.

### Step 7: Initialize physical protocol state

Initialize:

```text
tx_state = IDLE
tx_seq = 0
tx_log_chnl = 0
tx_hdr_cmd = 0
rx_fault_cnt = 0
tx_fault_cnt = 0
```

Initialize PWC logical-channel state to:

```text
in_used = 0
tx_state = IDLE
rx_isr = NULL
tx_isr = NULL
tx_cmpl_isr = NULL
```

### Step 8: Open PWC

Use:

```c
mb_chnl_open(0x12, NULL);
```

or the AP-side symbolic `MB_CHNL_PWC`.

### Step 9: Install callbacks

Install:

```c
mb_chnl_ctrl(
    MB_CHNL_PWC,
    MB_CHNL_SET_RX_ISR,
    cpu1_pwc_rx_isr
);

mb_chnl_ctrl(
    MB_CHNL_PWC,
    MB_CHNL_SET_TX_ISR,
    cpu1_pwc_tx_isr
);

mb_chnl_ctrl(
    MB_CHNL_PWC,
    MB_CHNL_SET_TX_CMPL_ISR,
    cpu1_pwc_tx_complete_isr
);
```

The TX and TX-complete callbacks may be no-ops for the minimal boot path, but the RX callback is essential.

### Step 10: Send boot-ready

Send:

```text
logical channel = 0x12
cmd              = PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD
param1           = 1
param2           = 0
param3           = 0
```

The reference AP performs this in `bk_pm_cp1_boot_ok_response_set()`.

# 14. CPU1 transmit sequence

For a command from CPU1 to CP0:

1. Build logical command:

```c
mb_chnl_cmd_t cmd = {0};

cmd.hdr.cmd = command;
cmd.hdr.state = 0;
cmd.param1 = p1;
cmd.param2 = p2;
cmd.param3 = p3;
```

2. Validate logical channel is `0x12`.
3. Reject if PWC channel is not open.
4. Reject or queue if PWC logical TX state is already busy.
5. Copy command into the logical channel's private four-word buffer.
6. Mark logical TX state BUSY.
7. If the physical CPU0 channel is IDLE:
   - mark physical channel BUSY;
   - increment `tx_seq`;
   - populate physical header:
     - `cmd`
     - `state = 0`
     - `ctrl = 0`
     - `tx_seq`
     - `logical_chnl = 0x12`
   - execute a data memory barrier;
   - copy/send the four-word physical payload.
8. If the physical channel is BUSY, leave the logical command pending.
9. On the hardware send:
   - select the next shared slot;
   - copy all 16 bytes;
   - write pointer and length to the CPU1 hardware FIFO;
   - write destination CPU ID 0 to `reg_0x24.mail_tid`.
10. Leave physical channel BUSY until a matching ACK is received.

The reference logical implementation copies the logical command and marks it busy at:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:867-875`

---

# 15. CPU1 receive/ACK sequence

For each received hardware FIFO entry:

1. Read source CPU ID and the two FIFO words.
2. Verify length is exactly 16.
3. Invalidate/flush the shared buffer if required.
4. Copy the four words locally.
5. Interpret word 0 as a physical header.
6. If `ctrl & CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX`:
   - process as ACK;
   - validate source/destination/logical channel;
   - validate sequence;
   - complete the outstanding transaction only on exact match.
7. Otherwise:
   - validate logical destination is CPU1;
   - validate source is CPU0;
   - validate logical channel index;
   - clear physical framing fields before calling the PWC callback;
   - call the PWC RX callback.
8. If the command is not synchronous:
   - restore the original physical header;
   - set `CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX`;
   - send the modified four-word buffer back to CPU0.
9. The ACK must be transmitted through CPU1's channel 1 FIFO with destination CPU0.

The callback is allowed to overwrite:

```text
param1 -> ack_data1
param2 -> ack_data2
param3 -> ack_data3/ack_state
```

The physical header restoration must preserve the original command and state while adding the ACK-box control bit.

# 16. ACK/state behavior needed by PWC

## 16.1 Command state

Normal PWC command:

```text
hdr.state = 0
```

The callback may use the command's three parameters to return command-specific status. The protocol-level ACK state is in the ACK header's four-bit `state` field.

## 16.2 ACK values

Use:

```text
ACK_STATE_PENDING  = 1
ACK_STATE_COMPLETE = 2
ACK_STATE_FAIL     = 3
```

These are defined at:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:129-134`

For a minimal boot-ready transport:

- `PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD` should receive a complete/success ACK.
- A recognized PWC command that was dispatched should receive complete or pending according to the CP-side expectation.
- An unsupported command should receive `ACK_STATE_FAIL`.
- An invalid logical channel or malformed payload should produce a failure ACK when possible; otherwise discard and count a protocol fault.

## 16.3 Sequence matching

The physical sequence is eight bits:

```text
tx_seq bits 23:16 of physical word 0
```

It increments per physical destination transaction and wraps naturally modulo 256.

The receiver must compare both:

```text
logical_chnl
tx_seq
```

against the currently outstanding transaction. Matching only the command ID is insufficient because multiple logical channels can use the same command ID and stale ACKs are possible after reset/recovery.

# 18. Essential boot-ready support

The following items are essential.

## Hardware

- BK7258 mbox0 base mapping.
- Channel-1 register access.
- Channel-1 FIFO configuration:
  - start 2;
  - length 3.
- Channel enable after start/length programming.
- Channel-1 normal interrupt enable.
- RX FIFO drain loop.
- CPU1 mailbox IRQ registration and CPU1 interrupt routing.
- 32-bit destination CPU ID writes to `mail_tid`.

## Shared memory

- Two or more 16-byte shared payload slots, or an equivalent lifetime-safe buffer scheme.
- Pointer/length hardware message.
- Length validation equal to 16.
- Cache maintenance or coherent mapping.
- Buffer lifetime protection until the receiver copies the payload.

## Protocol

- `mailbox_data_t`.
- `mb_chnl_hdr_t`.
- `mb_chnl_cmd_t`.
- `mb_chnl_ack_t`.
- Physical header with:
  - command;
  - state;
  - control;
  - sequence;
  - logical channel.
- `CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX`.
- `MB_CHNL_PWC = 0x12` on CPU1/AP.
- One outstanding physical transaction per destination.
- TX sequence increment and exact ACK sequence matching.
- ACK generation using the received command buffer.
- FIFO draining in the IRQ handler.

## PWC

- Open PWC logical channel.
- Install PWC RX callback.
- Send `PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD` with `param1 = 1`.
- Return an ACK for received PWC commands.
- Preserve all three PWC parameters.
- At minimum, recognize or safely fail commands needed during the initial CP/CPU1 boot exchange.

# 20. Important implementation hazards

## 20.1 Do not use the old two-box mailbox struct for PWC

The older structure:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/mailbox_struct.h:22-82`

contains:

```c
smb_devid
smb_verid
smb_clkrst
smb_state
box_ready
box_clear
sender
receiver
box0_param0..box0_param3
box1_param0..box1_param3
```

Its register base is also `SOC_MBOX0_REG_BASE`, but its semantics are not the active mbox0 v2 FIFO transport. The active PWC path is compiled through `mbox0_drv.c`, `mbox0_adapter.c`, and `mailbox_channel.c`.

## 20.2 Do not send the four-word protocol directly into the hardware FIFO

The hardware FIFO entry is not the four-word PWC packet. It is:

```text
word 0 = pointer to shared four-word payload
word 1 = 16
```

The four-word PWC packet is stored in shared memory and referenced by the FIFO pointer.

## 20.3 Do not reuse a shared slot too early

The adapter rotates two slots:

```c
mailbox_tx_box[dst] =
    (mailbox_tx_box[dst] + 1) % TX_BOX_NUM;
```

A NuttX implementation must preserve the same lifetime guarantee. The slot cannot be overwritten while its pointer remains queued or while the receiving CPU may still be reading it.

## 20.4 Do not acknowledge before copying the command

The receive path must copy the shared payload before the callback modifies it into ACK data. If the shared slot is reused before that copy, the command can be corrupted.

## 20.5 Do not clear the physical channel on arbitrary ACKs

An ACK is valid only if both the logical channel and sequence match the outstanding transaction. Otherwise, count/discard or perform controlled recovery.

## 20.6 Do not enable only the hardware interrupt

The hardware channel interrupt and CPU interrupt-controller route are separate. Both must be enabled. The reference sequence enables the channel interrupt and then calls the CPU/core interrupt group enable function.

## 20.7 Do not omit the FIFO drain loop

The IRQ must drain all available channel-1 entries. Processing one entry per IRQ can leave the FIFO asserted and interfere with subsequent PWC traffic.

## 20.8 Watch the callback ABI

The reference callback typedefs use:

```c
typedef void (*chnl_rx_isr_t)(void *param, mb_chnl_cmd_t *cmd_buf);
typedef void (*chnl_tx_isr_t)(void *param);
typedef void (*chnl_tx_cmpl_isr_t)(void *param, mb_chnl_ack_t *ack_buf);
```

The PWC source uses callbacks declared with `int *pm_mb` in the implementation, which is ABI-compatible with `void *` on the target but should be normalized in a clean NuttX port.

# 21. Minimal implementation contract

A NuttX CPU1 transport can be considered protocol-compatible when it satisfies this contract:

```c
struct bk7258_cpu1_mbox_transport {
    int  (*init)(void);
    int  (*send16)(const uint32_t words[4], uint8_t dst_cpu);
    void (*irq_handler)(int irq, void *context, void *arg);
};
```

Required wire behavior for `send16()`:

```text
1. Select a free 16-byte shared slot.
2. Store words[0..3] in the slot.
3. Perform release barrier/cache clean.
4. Check CPU0 receive FIFO not full.
5. Write shared slot address to CPU1 channel-1 TDATA0.
6. Write 16 to CPU1 channel-1 TDATA1.
7. Write destination CPU ID 0 to channel-1 TID.
8. Retain slot ownership until the receiver has consumed the pointed-to payload.
```

Required wire behavior for the IRQ:

```text
while channel-1 FIFO is not empty:
    read SID and two FIFO words
    validate length == 16
    invalidate shared payload if needed
    copy four words locally
    dispatch physical command or ACK
```

Required logical PWC behavior:

```text
CPU1 -> CPU0 logical channel: 0x12
CPU0 -> CPU1 logical channel: 0x42
```
